The Linux community is light years ahead from Microsoft.

Imagine for instance that I want to create a template file for Linux VMs. I prepare a kickstart (CentOS, Red Hat) or a preseed (Debian, Ubuntu) file and the installation runs automatically without human intervention. There is even the possibility of including some bash to polish the result! In minutes (because I can have my own local mirror), you get something ready for your config management tool (Puppet, Chef, Ansible). In less than 1 hour, you can deliver. The RedHat documentation is amazing, the Debian Sys Admin Manual is on par. Anything I need to know, is there or what I will find there will point me on the right direction. Straight to the point, no bullshit.

On the other hand, if I want to prepare a Windows template for VMs... It's a fucking nightmare. First, you need to create an unattended.xml file (good luck trying to do that after checking the sea of misinformation and half truths around), run the installation/update process that will take forever, run a sysprep that will let the machine ready for another sysprep that will run the first time you boot the machine. The process can be barely automated and it seems like at chez Microsoft, they enjoy wasting our time. The documentation contains 0 useful information, trial and error is the only way forward. And the trials take way too long.

And let's not talk about containers, µS has not figured out them yet.
